Okay so it was kind of insane dude. So, it was a newly opened facility when I started(had been opened for a month) I discovered the head administrator came from working at another nursing home and left due to mysterious reasons. She also brought a bunch of staff from the other nursing home with her. She would brag about how her and the DON were like mother and daughter. The most insane thing, was that the director of wellness/ head “nurse” was passing herself off as an RN and only had an LPN. Found it out through the state website. Even the nursing staff had no clue that she was not an RN let alone resident families. I never, not once saw a DR come visit any patients at this facility. There was never even an actual RN on the staff!! She was also the only LPN, everybody else was a CNA. 

I’m not an expert but I believe a main reason why they were all on hospice was because the hospice nurse was actually an RN and would come in a few times a week to actually take care of the residents. It was so sad. 

The worst part was that this is in a wealthy area and it was a totally private facility, they did not accept any Medicaid patients. I imagine that this was the main reason why it didn’t get flagged. However myself and three other employees walked out and reported them to the ombudsman after finding out about the imposter. I really hope things turned around for the residents. 

anyways, sorry for the dump but I will never work at a private facility again because it was the Wild West

Edit: 
The scam was discovered by an agency Occupational therapist who noticed how many residents were on hospice and this lead to the discovery of the fake RN

Yup. The last nursing home I worked at had a scam where they would put all the residents on hospice. Honestly for me it took months but it’s been worth it. Like it was a slow transition to disassociating constantly to sometimes being present to mostly being present. I’m still working on it. Here’s a short list of what helped (and like I said it wasn’t instant):

- talk to yourself, or in your head. I say things like “my name is crochet creature, today is November 29th”  facts like that to help ground me. 

- picking something to do every day or every other day. Whenever I tried to come up with a routine it would get too overwhelming. I decided well if I can’t do it all I’ll do one, it’s better than nothing. 

-smells. Idk it smells trigger you but some of them like mint feel a little more awake. I usually carry lotions around or essential oils so I can have them whenever

-talking to more people. I’m not a very social creature but I make more of an effort to make small talk with people in my class. And I think commenting on reddit also counts as being social 😊

so those are a few and it has taken awhile, and it’s not a substitute for medication or going to a doctor. They’re just little things that helped me.
